Title: Diagnosis of test `testJiraLang281` failure in `DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod`

Details:
- The test `testJiraLang281` checks the difference in months between December 31, 2005, and October 6, 2006, expecting the result `"09"`.
- The method under test `DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long startMillis, long endMillis, String format)` delegates to the overloaded method which also includes timezone and zero-padding options.
- Inside `formatPeriod`, the difference in time is broken down into years, months, days, hours, minutes, seconds, and milliseconds by using Calendar fields.
- An important part is the calculation of the days difference (`int days = end.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH) - start.get(Calendar.DAY_OF_MONTH);`) and then adjusting when under 0 by adding a fixed 31 days: 
  ```java
  while (days < 0) {
      days += 31;
      months -= 1;
  }
  ```
- This part stands out because adding a fixed 31 days does not account for variable month lengths in the calendar (some months have 30 or 28/29 days).
- This can cause the computed month difference to be off by one, leading to the unexpected value from the test.
- The test expects 9 months difference (from December 31, 2005 to October 6, 2006), but due to adding 31 days regardless of actual month length, the calculation likely yields 10 months or another incorrect value.
- Other parts of the method involve "normalizing" the remainder of the fields by calling `reduceAndCorrect` and some logic to add months if years aren't requested or days if months aren't requested. These appear to be less likely causing the immediate failure.
- The root issue comes from the simplistic handling of day difference adjustment when days < 0 by just adding 31 days without considering the actual number of days in the previous month.

Next step would be to fix this logic to correctly handle the variable length of months when adjusting the days difference.

Classes and methods most relevant to fix:
- `DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long,long,String,boolean,TimeZone)`
org.apache.commons.lang.time.DurationFormatUtils.formatPeriod(long,long,String,boolean,TimeZone)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
